papers.title: Polystyrene Nanoparticles Cause Sex-Specific Toxicity in Male Zebrafish, Which Can Be Mitigated by Melatonin.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoparticles caused sex-specific reproductive and brain toxicity in male zebrafish, which melatonin co-treatment relieved.

papers.title: Polystyrene Nanoplastics Induce DNA Damage and Excitotoxicity in Whole-Brain Organoids: The Role of the TLR9/MyD88 Pathway.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics of 50 nm induced DNA damage and excitotoxicity in human whole-brain organoids through the TLR9 and MyD88 pathway.

papers.title: Oral exposure of polystyrene microplastics and doxycycline affects mice neurological function via gut microbiota disruption: The orchestrating role of fecal microbiota transplantation.
papers.summary: Polystyrene microplastics with a diameter of less than 5 mm with doxycycline disturbed mouse neurological function through gut microbiota disruption, which FMT reversed.

papers.title: Inhibiting ferroptosis in brain microvascular endothelial cells: A potential strategy to mitigate polystyrene nanoplastics‒induced blood‒brain barrier dysfunction.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics raised blood-brain barrier permeability and lowered ZO-1, which a glutathione-dependent ferroptosis inhibitor relieved.

papers.title: Oxidized/unmodified-polyethylene microplastics neurotoxicity in mice: Perspective from microbiota-gut-brain axis.
papers.summary: Oxidised polyethylene microplastics impaired the microbiota-gut-brain axis in mice, with probiotic supplementation easing the cognitive and intestinal damage.

papers.title: Polyethylene microplastics differently induced gut microbiota dysbiosis and hepatic metabolism in male and female adult zebrafish.
papers.journal: Comp Biochem Physiol C Toxicol Pharmacol
papers.summary: Polyethylene microplastics induced sex-specific gut microbiota and hepatic metabolic changes in adult zebrafish, with females taking longer to recover.

papers.title: Microplastics induce insulin resistance by causing mitochondrial dysfunction associated with mROS in skeletal muscle in vitro.
papers.summary: Microplastics caused mitochondrial dysfunction and insulin resistance in human skeletal muscle cells through mitochondrial reactive oxygen species.

papers.title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress exacerbates microplastics-induced toxicity in animal cells.
papers.summary: Polystyrene microplastics lowered viability and damaged morphology of goat mammary epithelial cells through endoplasmic reticulum stress.

papers.title: Oxidative stress-activated Nrf2 remitted polystyrene nanoplastic-induced mitochondrial damage and inflammatory response in HepG2 cells.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics damaged HepG2 mitochondria and activated inflammatory signalling through Nrf2, remitted by N-acetylcysteine.

papers.title: The size-dependence and reversibility of polystyrene nanoplastics-induced lipid accumulation in mice: Possible roles of lysosomes.
papers.summary: Long-term polystyrene nanoplastic exposure accumulated lipids in mouse liver, more so in 100 nm than 500 nm particles, and lysosomal exocytosis cleared them.

papers.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics-induced lung apoptosis and ferroptosis via ROS-dependent endoplasmic reticulum stress.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics drove lung cell apoptosis and ferroptosis through reactive oxygen species dependent endoplasmic reticulum stress, eased by N-acetylcysteine.

papers.title: Exploring Oxidative Stress and Metabolic Dysregulation in Lung Tissues of Offspring Rats Exposed to Prenatal Polystyrene Microplastics: Effects of Melatonin Treatment.
papers.summary: Prenatal polystyrene microplastics caused lung oxidative stress and metabolic dysregulation in rat offspring, improved by melatonin treatment.

papers.title: Ferritinophagy Mediated by Oxidative Stress-Driven Mitochondrial Damage Is Involved in the Polystyrene Nanoparticles-Induced Ferroptosis of Lung Injury.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoparticles caused ferritinophagy-driven ferroptosis and lung injury across cells, mice and a lung-on-a-chip, relieved by ferrostatin and N-acetylcysteine.

papers.title: Toxic effects of nanoplastics with different sizes and surface charges on epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in A549 cells and the potential toxicological mechanism.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics of differing size and charge induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition in human alveolar cells, reversed by NOX4 knock-down.

papers.title: Integrated Biomarker, Histopathological and Genotoxicity-Based Toxicological Evaluation of Polystyrene and Polyethylene Microplastics in Oreochromis mossambicus.
papers.summary: Microplastics of 3 size fractions accumulated in tilapia tissues and raised oxidative stress, genotoxicity and histopathological change.

papers.title: Exposure of polystyrene nanoplastics led to ferroptosis on cardiomyocytes.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics of 100 nm raised mitochondrial ROS and induced ferroptosis and iron overload in cardiomyocytes.

papers.title: Inhibiting ferroptosis in brain microvascular endothelial cells: A potential strategy to mitigate polystyrene nanoplastics‒induced blood‒brain barrier dysfunction.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics raised blood-brain barrier permeability and lowered ZO-1, which a glutathione-dependent ferroptosis inhibitor relieved.

papers.title: Effects of polystyrene nanoplastics on endothelium senescence and its underlying mechanism.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics drove premature senescence of coronary artery endothelial cells through redox-sensitive eNOS and Sirt1 signalling, eased by resveratrol.

papers.title: Inhaled polystyrene nanoparticles may cause fibrotic lesions via immune dysregulation and energy metabolism disturbance.
papers.summary: Ninety days of inhaled polystyrene nanoparticles produced fibrotic lung lesions in mice through immune dysregulation and energy metabolism disturbance.

papers.title: Polystyrene microplastics impact on cardiac and pulmonary physiology and microenvironment in a mouse model: Role of taurine supplementation and molecular docking insights.
papers.summary: Sixty days of polystyrene microplastics damaged cardiac and pulmonary physiology in mice, with taurine supplementation easing the oxidative and inflammatory burden.

papers.title: Histopathological and intestinal microbial changes in crayfish (Procambarus clarkii) after exposure to polyethylene nanoparticles (PE-NPS) and their remediation by Spirulina platensis.
papers.summary: Polyethylene nanoparticles damaged crayfish tissue and altered intestinal microbiota, which Spirulina platensis remedied.

papers.title: Nanoplastics exposure accelerates the progression of osteoarthritis via lysosomal destabilization-mediated pyroptosis.
papers.summary: Nanoplastics accelerated osteoarthritis progression in mice through lysosomal destabilisation mediated pyroptosis.

papers.title: Polyethylene nanoplastics promote tumor progression in canine mammary tumor U27 cells via the PPARγ-NF-κB axis.
papers.summary: Polyethylene nanoplastics promoted canine mammary tumour cell progression through the PPAR-gamma NF-kappaB axis.

papers.title: Dust Fall Microplastics from a Megacity of China Inhibit Autophagy via the PI3K/Akt/mTOR Pathway.
papers.summary: Microplastics from dust fall in Xi'an inhibited autophagy and induced apoptosis in macrophages through PI3K, Akt and mTOR signalling, reversed by half the particles.

papers.title: Ototoxicity of polystyrene nanoplastics in mice, HEI-OC1 cells and zebrafish.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics damaged mouse and zebrafish hair cells and raised ototoxic thresholds, with HEI-OC1 cells apoptosis, ferroptosis and inflammation.

papers.title: In vivo hepatic effects and post-exposure recovery following polyethylene terephthalate microplastic ingestion in Swiss Albino mice (Mus musculus).
papers.summary: Fourteen days of PET microplastic ingestion caused hepatic oxidative injury in Swiss albino mice, with partial recovery after a depuration period.

papers.title: Chronic exposure to polystyrene microplastics at environmentally relevant concentration induced growth retardation in Macrobrachium rosenbergii via multi-pathway toxicity: Oxidative stress, microbial dysbiosis, and biodistribution.
papers.summary: Forty-two days of environmentally relevant polystyrene microplastics at 1 mg/L retarded growth in juvenile freshwater prawns via oxidative stress and microbial dysbiosis.

papers.summary: Polyethylene microplastics induced sex-specific gut microbiota and hepatic metabolic changes in adult zebrafish, with females taking longer to recover.

papers.title: Hepatotoxic Mechanisms of Polyethylene Terephthalate Microplastics Revealed by Network Toxicology, Molecular Docking, and In Vivo Validation.
papers.summary: Network toxicology, docking and in vivo validation showed PET microplastics harm the liver through PI3K and AKT signalling, reversed by an agonist.

papers.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics trigger ferroptosis-dependent liver injury caused by ACSL4 overaccumulation.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics triggered ferroptosis-dependent liver injury through ACSL4 overaccumulation in AML12 cells and mice.

papers.summary: Polyethylene nanoparticles damaged crayfish tissue and altered intestinal microbiota, which Spirulina platensis remedied.

papers.title: Chronic exposure to polystyrene microplastics induces renal fibrosis via ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Six months of drinking water polystyrene microplastics caused renal fibrosis in mice through amino-functionalised particles and epithelial ferroptosis.

papers.title: Protective efficacy of dietary natural antioxidants on microplastic particles-induced histopathological lesions in African catfish (Clarias gariepinus).
papers.summary: Dietary natural antioxidants reversed microplastic histopathological lesions in African catfish, suggesting a protective effect.

papers.title: Investigation of nephrotoxicity on mice exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics and the potential amelioration effects of DHA-enriched phosphatidylserine.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics of 100 nm caused murine nephrotoxicity, which DHA-enriched phosphatidylserine ameliorated.

papers.title: Combined exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics and bisphenol A results in mitochondrial damage and ferroptosis via the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway in mice kidneys.
papers.summary: Six weeks of polystyrene nanoplastics with bisphenol A damaged mouse kidneys through mitochondrial damage, ferroptosis and PI3K-AKT signalling.

papers.title: Changes in haematology, metabolic rate, and cellular structure of spleen and head kidney of brown trout, Salmo trutta, after exposure to polystyrene microplastic particles.
papers.summary: Thirty days of dietary polystyrene changed haematology, metabolic rate and spleen and kidney structure in brown trout.

papers.title: Deleterious effects of polypropylene released from paper cups on blood profile and liver tissue of Clarias gariepinus: bioremediation using Spirulina.
papers.summary: Polypropylene released from paper cups altered blood profile and liver tissue in African catfish, improving after 45 days of recovery.

papers.title: Melatonin and probiotics ameliorate nanoplastics-induced hematopoietic injury by modulating the gut microbiota-metabolism.
papers.summary: Nanoplastics suppressed bone marrow haematopoietic stem cell renewal and differentiation, ameliorated by melatonin or probiotics modulating the microbiota.

papers.title: Assessment of the effect of long-term exposure to microplastics and depuration period in Sparus aurata Linnaeus, 1758: Liver and blood biomarkers.
papers.summary: Ninety days of low density polyethylene microplastic diet raised liver and plasma oxidative stress and inflammation biomarkers in gilthead seabream, partly reversed after depuration.

papers.title: Changes in haematology, metabolic rate, and cellular structure of spleen and head kidney of brown trout, Salmo trutta, after exposure to polystyrene microplastic particles.
papers.summary: Thirty days of dietary polystyrene changed haematology, metabolic rate and spleen and kidney structure in brown trout.

papers.title: Taurine attenuates polystyrene microplastic-associated oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptotic changes in the spleen of mice.
papers.summary: Sixty days of polystyrene microplastics caused oxidative stress, inflammation and apoptotic change in mouse spleen, which taurine attenuated.

papers.title: The presence of microplastics in human semen and the protective role of nicotinamide mononucleotide against polystyrene nanoplastics-induced reproductive and early embryonic toxicity.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics damaged human sperm function and mouse embryo development, and nicotinamide mononucleotide eased the damage.

papers.title: Polyethylene nanoplastics promote tumor progression in canine mammary tumor U27 cells via the PPARγ-NF-κB axis.
papers.summary: Polyethylene nanoplastics promoted canine mammary tumour cell progression through the PPAR-gamma NF-kappaB axis.

papers.title: Removal and toxic intervention of polystyrene microplastics and nanoplastics by magnetic nano-Fe3O4 in spermatogonial GC-1 cells.
papers.summary: Magnetic iron oxide relieved polystyrene nanoplastic toxicity in spermatogonial GC-1 cells after removal.

papers.title: Protective Effects and Potential Mechanisms of D-Aspartate on Testicular Damage Induced by Polystyrene Microplastics.
papers.summary: Polystyrene microplastics damaged rat testes through oxidative stress, apoptosis and autophagy, and the amino acid D-aspartate reversed the damage.

papers.title: Epidermal and dermal cell-composed organospheres to assess microplastic-induced skin toxicity.
papers.summary: Epidermal and dermal cell organospheres were used to test microplastic-induced skin toxicity, validating a high-throughput screening system.

papers.title: Surface charge-dependent toxicity of polystyrene nanoplastics in human lung epithelial BEAS-2B and HaCaT cells.
papers.summary: Surface charge determined polystyrene nanoplastic toxicity in human lung BEAS-2B and skin HaCaT cells.

papers.title: Polystyrene and polyvinyl chloride microplastics exposure induces ocular surface inflammation by causing mitochondrial damage and lipid metabolic disruption.
papers.summary: Polystyrene and PVC microplastics caused ocular surface inflammation in human cells by damaging mitochondria and disrupting lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Exposure of human corneal epithelial cells to microplastic particles induces a phase-specific cytokine response.
papers.summary: Microplastic particles produced from grinding polyethylene eyedrop vials provoked phase-specific cytokine responses in human corneal epithelial cells.

papers.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics induce ocular surface toxicity via endoplasmic reticulum stress.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics caused ocular surface toxicity in mice and human corneal epithelial cells through endoplasmic reticulum stress.

papers.title: Exposure to high dose of polystyrene nanoplastics causes trophoblast cell apoptosis and induces miscarriage.
papers.summary: High dose polystyrene nanoplastics caused human trophoblast apoptosis and miscarriage, which Bcl-2 supplementation relieved.

papers.title: Polystyrene Nanoparticles Disrupt Oxidative Phosphorylation and Impair Placental Development in Mice.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoparticles disrupted oxidative phosphorylation in the mouse placenta and impaired placental development.

papers.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics perturb trophoblastic copper homeostasis with reduced ATP7B expression.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics perturbed copper homeostasis in trophoblast cells and human placental tissue, with less ATP7B and more copper accumulation.

papers.title: Gut microbiota contributes to polystyrene nanoplastics-induced fetal growth restriction by disturbing placental nicotinamide metabolism.
papers.summary: Gut microbiota disturbed placental nicotinamide metabolism by polystyrene nanoplastics, restricting fetal growth in mice.

papers.title: Maternal exposure to polystyrene microplastics alters placental metabolism in mice.
papers.summary: Maternal polystyrene microplastics altered placental metabolism in mice, with lower lysine and glucose in the placenta at the highest concentration.

papers.title: The presence of microplastics in human semen and the protective role of nicotinamide mononucleotide against polystyrene nanoplastics-induced reproductive and early embryonic toxicity.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics damaged human sperm function and mouse embryo development, and nicotinamide mononucleotide eased the damage.

papers.title: Mitigative potential of kaempferide against polyethylene microplastics induced testicular damage by activating Nrf-2/Keap-1 pathway.
papers.summary: Polyethylene microplastics lowered Nrf2 and antioxidant enzymes in rat testes, and the flavonol kaempferide abrogated the oxidative and testicular damage.

papers.title: Polyethylene Terephthalate Microplastic Exposure Induced Reproductive Toxicity Through Oxidative Stress and p38 Signaling Pathway Activation in Male Mice.
papers.summary: PET microplastic exposure damaged testicular tissue and lowered sperm quality in male mice through oxidative stress and p38 signalling.

papers.title: Pinostrobin alleviates testicular and spermatological damage induced by polystyrene microplastics in adult albino rats.
papers.summary: Polystyrene microplastics damaged rat testes and sperm, and the flavonoid pinostrobin reduced the oxidative and inflammatory injury.

papers.title: Probiotics improve polystyrene microplastics-induced male reproductive toxicity in mice by alleviating inflammatory response.
papers.summary: Probiotics improved polystyrene microplastic-induced male reproductive injury in mice by easing inflammation along a gut microbiota and testis axis.

papers.title: The role of gut microbiota in mediating increased toxicity of nano-sized polystyrene compared to micro-sized polystyrene in mice.
papers.summary: Nano-sized polystyrene was more toxic than micro-sized in mice, and depleting the gut microbiota with antibiotics relieved the damage and inflammation.

papers.title: Long-term low-dose exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics induces morphological and transcriptional reprogramming to enhance metastatic potential of colorectal cancer cells.
papers.summary: Long-term low-dose polystyrene nanoplastics changed morphology and gene expression in colorectal cancer cells, raising migration and metastasis gene expression.

papers.title: Ingestion of a human-relevant mixture of environmentally sourced microplastics promotes inflammation and tumorigenesis in the mouse colon.
papers.summary: Ingestion of a human-relevant mixture of environmentally sourced microplastics promoted inflammation and tumorigenesis in the mouse colon.

papers.title: Polystyrene microplastics exposure increases the disruption of intestinal barrier integrity and gut microbiota homeostasis during obesity and aging.
papers.summary: Chronic low-dose polystyrene microplastics worsened intestinal barrier disruption and gut microbiota homeostasis in obese and ageing mice, which oral Akkermansia muciniphila restored.

papers.title: Colonic Barrier Dysfunction and Inflammation Induced by Nano-/Micro-Plastics Fibers in Mice via the FAK/NF-κB/iNOS and TLR4/NF-κB/iNOS Pathways.
papers.summary: Nano and microplastic fibres both raised colonic NF-kB and iNOS and damaged the barrier in mice, the larger particles more so, through FAK and TLR4.

papers.title: Probiotics improve polystyrene microplastics-induced male reproductive toxicity in mice by alleviating inflammatory response.
papers.summary: Probiotics improved polystyrene microplastic-induced male reproductive injury in mice by easing inflammation along a gut microbiota and testis axis.

papers.title: Oral Exposure to Polystyrene Nanoplastics Disrupts Gut-Testis Metabolic Homeostasis and EGR1-Associated Steroidogenic Regulation in Male Mice.
papers.summary: Oral polystyrene nanoplastics disrupted gut-testis metabolic homeostasis in male mice through EGR1 and steroidogenic regulation.

papers.title: Low-dose polystyrene microplastics exposure increases susceptibility to obesity-induced MASLD via disrupting intestinal barrier integrity and gut microbiota homeostasis.
papers.summary: Low-dose polystyrene microplastics made mice more susceptible to obesity-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease through intestinal barrier and gut microbiota disruption.

papers.title: Associations between microplastics in human feces and colorectal cancer risk.
papers.summary: Case-control study of 258 patients found higher faecal microplastic concentrations associated with colorectal cancer risk, with a nonlinear dose-response.

papers.title: In vivo exposure of mixed microplastic particles in mice and its impacts on the murine gut microbiome and metabolome.
papers.summary: Four weeks of mixed microplastic gavage altered the murine gut microbiome and serum metabolome, with sex and dose dependence.

papers.title: Effects of polystyrene nanoplastics on endothelium senescence and its underlying mechanism.
papers.summary: Polystyrene nanoplastics drove premature senescence of coronary artery endothelial cells through redox-sensitive eNOS and Sirt1 signalling, eased by resveratrol.

papers.title: Polystyrene Microplastics Induce Sustained Cardiovascular Redox Imbalance and Alter Mitochondrial Quality Control.
papers.summary: Repeated oral polystyrene microplastics produced sustained cardiovascular redox imbalance and mitochondrial quality control changes in rats.

papers.title: The mechanism of vascular injury caused by polystyrene microplastics: Involving ferroptosis and metabolomics.
papers.summary: Polystyrene microplastics injured mouse vessels through oxidative stress, ferroptosis and metabolomic disturbance, eased by a ferroptosis inhibitor.

papers.title: Maternal gestational and lactational exposure to polystyrene nanoplastics triggers vascular injury and lipid deposition in mouse offspring.
papers.summary: Maternal polystyrene nanoplastic exposure in mice caused vascular injury and lipid deposition in offspring, resolved only partially by nine weeks.

papers.title: The cardiovascular toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in rats: based on untargeted metabolomics analysis.
papers.summary: Untargeted metabolomics suggested long-term polystyrene microplastic exposure damaged myocardial tissue in rats through oxidative and inflammatory pathways.

papers.summary: Fourteen days of PET microplastic ingestion caused hepatic oxidative injury in Swiss albino mice, with partial recovery after a depuration period.

papers.summary: Microplastics caused mitochondrial dysfunction and insulin resistance in human skeletal muscle cells through mitochondrial reactive oxygen species.

papers.title: Ferroptosis participated in inhaled polystyrene nanoplastics-induced liver injury and fibrosis.
papers.summary: Inhaled 40 nm polystyrene nanoplastics caused liver injury and fibrosis in mice through ferroptosis, eased by the ferroptosis inhibitor Fer-1.
